results.summary: The referencing design sections are highly consistent with the definition of {META_ConfigurableSystem}. The referencing design sections are highly consistent with the definition of {META_3TierSeparation}. The 3-tier decomposition (Tier 1: Primary/Architecture, Tier 2: Decomposed Subcomponent, Tier 3: Leaf/Implementation) is applied uniformly across all component classifications, and the dependency flow (downward decomposition and upward refinement) is explicitly maintained.

The implementation of {META_RecoveryStrategy} is highly consistent across all referencing sections. The definition of returning recovery actions instead of error codes is strictly followed, and the four specific strategies (ignore, retry, restart, panic) are uniformly defined and applied across the WIT interfaces, system services, and runtime components.

The keyword {GLOBAL_StaticScalability} is consistently applied across all referencing sections. The design implements the requirement of eliminating dynamic overhead by using compile-time constants for resource limits, memory pools, and container capacities.

The referencing design sections are perfectly consistent with the definition of {META_BinarySearch} and consistent with each other. The implementation of O(log n) search via flat_map_view and flat_set_view is uniformly described across the JIT pipeline, system containers, and JIT runtime components.

The specification for {FlatViewNarrowing} is highly consistent across all referencing sections. The definition of narrowing as a monotonic reduction of a non-owning view is correctly implemented in the JIT pipeline, the system container vocabulary, and the debugger's breakpoint management.

The design sections are highly consistent with the definition of {IPCRouter}. All referencing components (Logging, IPC Router, System Service, and HAL) correctly implement the invariant that all system calls and inter-component communications must pass through the IPC Router for routing and access control.

The design sections are highly consistent with the {META_FaultIsolation} definition. The specification for {RoleBasedAccessControl} is highly consistent across all definition and design sections. The static role matrix is defined concretely in the configuration and implemented consistently in the IPC router's lookup pipeline and sequence diagrams.

The specification for {OwnershipTransfer} is highly consistent across all referencing sections. The abstract requirement of logical ownership movement to avoid copying is concretely implemented via a 3-stage (Revoke -> Enqueue -> Grant) state machine, which is consistently applied in the IPC Router, the vMMIO runtime, and the platform memory lifecycle.

The design sections are highly consistent with the {GLOBAL_Policy_Memory} definition. All referencing components strictly adhere to the prohibition of dynamic heap allocation (malloc/new) and implement the required alternatives (static pools, placement new, and non-owning views).

The specification for {ThreadedInterpreter} is highly consistent across all referencing design sections. The calling convention, register assignments, and architectural approach (CPS, __fastcall, and stack model) are uniformly described.

results.summary: Critical contradictions found in the physical implementation of the JIT Copy-and-Patch mechanism, specifically regarding register assignments and instruction logic between the Stencil Catalog and the Instruction Set specification.

issues.description: Contradiction in physical instruction implementation for 'i32.eqz' (0x45). The Stencil Catalog defines the implementation as 'cmp r4, #0; it eq; moveq r4, #1; it ne; movne r4, #0', whereas the Instruction Set specification defines it as 'RSBS r4, r4, #1; SBC r4, r4, r4'. These are fundamentally different Thumb-2 sequences.

Contradiction in register operand order for binary operations. The Stencil Catalog consistently uses 'r4' as TOS and 'r5' as NOS with the pattern 'op r4, r5, r4' (e.g., i32.add: 'adds r4, r5, r4'), while the Instruction Set specification defines the physical action as 'op r4, r4, r5' (e.g., i32.add: 'ADDS r4, r4, r5'). This reverses the source/destination relationship for non-commutative operations (like sub, div, shr).

Unbacked Verification Claim: The section claims the 'Zero Compile Cost Theorem' is measured via 'benchmarks/jit_zero_compile_cost_bench.py', but the provided text does not include the results or the log of this benchmark to substantiate the claim that execution time scales linearly.

issues.description: The text explicitly admits a 'known divergence' (既知の乖離) where the current implementation in `ipc_router_concept.py` is still dictionary-based and has not yet migrated to `flat_map_view`, contradicting the design claim of using sorted arrays for O(log N) lookup.

The 'Narrow-then-Search' mechanism claims a complexity of O(log n) where n is the narrowed range. While this is mathematically correct for the search phase, the total complexity is O(Cost of Narrowing + log n). The specification does not define the complexity of the 'coarse index' (粗い索引) lookup used for narrowing, leaving the total latency bound slightly ambiguous compared to the strict O(log N) requirement in the definition.
